To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the CTP 2PI effective action is stationary with respect to the CTP correlation functions, (2) the stationary CTP 2 PI effective action is a functional of the mean fields and correlation functions, and (3) the equations of motion for the correlation functions can be obtained from the stationary CTP effective action by functional differentiation.

(1) the CTP effective-action approach to quantum fields is the correct way to describe the statistical properties of nonequilbrium quantum systems, and (2) this approach can be used to derive the BBGKY hierarchy of quantum fields.
the CTP 2PI effective action is a useful tool to describe interacting quantum fields out of equilibrium.

the development of a quantum-field-theoretical framework for the description of dissipative phenomena in many-particle quantum systems.
the development and application of a quantum-statistical theory for the description of nonequilibrium phenomena in quantum field systems.

we provide a systematic and rigorous way to derive kinetic equations for quantum fields from a microscopic theory.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of interactions and at finite temperature, the quantum-field theory is inherently nonequilibrium.
